# Data used

```{r}
survey_data <- tribble(
  ~Country,      ~Wave, ~StartYear, ~EndYear,
  "Ethiopia",    "Wave 4", 2018, 2018,
  "Ethiopia",    "Wave 5", 2021, 2021,
  "Malawi",      "Wave 1", 2010, 2010,
  "Malawi",      "Wave 2", 2013, 2013,
  "Malawi",      "Wave 3", 2016, 2016,
  "Malawi",      "Wave 4", 2019, 2019,
  "Tanzania",    "Wave 4", 2014, 2014,
  "Tanzania",    "Wave 5", 2020, 2021
)
ggplot(survey_data, aes(x = StartYear, xend = EndYear, 
                        y = fct_rev(factor(Country)), 
                        yend = fct_rev(factor(Country)))) +
  geom_label(aes(x = StartYear, label = Wave), 
            size = 5, fill="#D4FF1D", color="blue", angle=65) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2010, 2021, by = 1),
                     limits = c(2008, 2022) ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16, color = "blue"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle = 45, hjust = 1, color = "blue"))
```

# Ethiopia

## Basic descriptives

There are **`r sum(dfeth$wave=="wave4")`** households in Ethiopian Social Survey (ESS) dataset who have produced maize as a main crop both in ESS4 and ESS5. In 2017, **`r sum(dfeth$rotation == "rotation" & dfeth$wave == "wave4")`** farmers have indicated that they have planted a legume on the maize plot during the past three years, and **`r sum(dfeth$rotation == "rotation" & dfeth$wave == "wave4" & dfeth$improved_maize == "improved")`** (**`r round(sum(dfeth$rotation == "rotation" & dfeth$wave == "wave4" & dfeth$improved_maize == "improved") / sum(dfeth$rotation == "rotation" & dfeth$wave == "wave4") * 100, 1)`**%) of them have also used improved maize seeds during the current cropping season. In 2020, the number of farmers adopting crop rotation has increased to **`r sum(dfeth$rotation == "rotation" & dfeth$wave == "wave5")`**, and also the number of those adopters who used improved maize seeds have increased to **`r sum(dfeth$rotation == "rotation" & dfeth$wave == "wave5" & dfeth$improved_maize == "improved")`** (**`r round(sum(dfeth$rotation == "rotation" & dfeth$wave == "wave5" & dfeth$improved_maize == "improved") / sum(dfeth$rotation == "rotation" & dfeth$wave == "wave5") * 100, 1)`**%).

The data reveals significant changes in adoption rates between 2017 and 2020. The number of farmers practicing maize-legume rotations and using improved seeds increased substantially over this period. Overall, adoption of improved seeds has grown considerably, with many more farmers implementing legume rotation on their maize plots.

::: {style="width:60%; background-color: #FDFDF6; padding: 12px "}
```{r}
dfeth |> 
  count(wave, improved_maize, rotation) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = rotation, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |> 
  kable(
    caption = "Table 1: Legume rotation and improved maize adoption in Ethiopia.",
    align = "llcc"
  )
```
:::

# Malawi

## Basic descriptives

In terms of legume rotation, there are obvious differences when comparing Wave 1 and Wave 2 with Wave 3 and Wave 4. This is because of the way the rotation variable was developed in these waves. In wave 1 an 2, we were only able to identify if legume was planted in the dry season following the maize cultivation in the dry season. However, in wave 3 and 4, farmers were asked what crops were planted following the previous rainy season[^1] as well as what crops will be planted after the next rainy season.

[^1]: That is the dry season before the reference rainy season.

::: {.column width="45%; background-color: #FDFDF6; padding: 12px "}

# Methods

## Ethiopia

In the analysis of Ethiopian maize-producing households from waves 4 and 5 of the Ethiopia Socioeconomic Survey (ESS), we focus exclusively on legume rotations. Maize-legume intercropping is not considered in this part due to its rare occurrence among the sampled households.
Our main variable, agroecological intensification, captures maize-legume rotations and improved maize cultivation practices. The variable of interest takes four values:

* **1: No intensification**
* **2: Maize-legume rotation**
* **3: Improved variety**
* **4: Maize-legume rotation with improved maize variety**

The table below presents the social and plot-level characteristics considered in the analyses. Plot characteristics reflect the attributes of plots where maize is the primary crop.

::: {style="background-color: #FDFDF6; padding: 12px "}
```{r}
table(dfeth$wave, dfeth$agr_intens) |> 
  kable(
    caption = "Table 4: Agroecological intensification in Ethiopia",
    align = "lcc")
```
:::
